method.windows: Half-open intervals using telemetry sim_time_seconds; post-step states carry zero-based evaluator step timestamps.
method.heading: Unwrap yaw from root quaternion [w,x,y,z] and sum adjacent signed increments within each window.
method.tracking: Body-frame velocity, matched to measured command in every row.
method.configuration: Random push disabled and episode length extended to 65 s; other training randomizations and observation corruption retained.

findings: All six cases completed with complete telemetry and no done/timeout events.
Direct zero-command standing shows persistent forward drift, whereas forward/backward stop tails are near zero mean longitudinal speed.
Pure left and right yaw commands do not produce sustained yaw tracking in the tested steady windows.
Compare moving-turn yaw tracking with the pure-turn windows; a turn while translating is not proof of in-place turning.
limitations: Single checkpoint, one seed, one environment, 20 seconds per case; not a general robustness claim.
No paired old-checkpoint rerun under the repaired observation semantics; observation repair and reward changes were trained together, so causes cannot be isolated.
Native only; exported JIT/ONNX parity and MuJoCo transfer were not evaluated.
No foot-contact force time series in these telemetry files; illegal-contact termination signals do not establish foot contact quality.
Transient HDR texture upload error appears in the first formal console; sampled videos show the robot.
All six videos decode to 999 frames / 19.98 seconds; all six telemetry files contain 1000 samples.
